decisions.reason: As a 2023 launch that stayed on the home page and sits very close to our core dosimetry offering, it carries visible commitment and strong strategic fit, so management would continue backing it.

This oncology risk management software builds directly on our established QA platform direction and, given our software integration capabilities and prior launch commitment, we would keep investing rather than reverse course early.
The CT image quality test phantom fits our medical imaging QA trajectory and is too recent a 2024 launch for weak early evidence to outweigh the resources and public commitment already made.

Although more distant from our traditional offer, the mammography image quality phantom extends our imaging QA presence and management would likely treat any initial uncertainty as temporary after committing it to market in 2024.

The full field mammography test phantom is also a recent, publicly launched extension into imaging QA, and escalation of commitment makes us more likely to continue and justify that expansion than to withdraw immediately.
Medical imaging QA instruments are aligned with our announced convergence of measurement, integration, and automation, so the strategic centrality and recent investment favor retaining the product.
